facts.fact: Nellimala's stone footings lie on a slope near the shore under lantana; the Thurai camp there has 63 tents, three horse lines (22, 26, 24 animals), about 40-50 barley sacks, three sentries at the track end, and a half-built siege tower of ship timber on a cart bed, three men high.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Neela to count tents, horse lines and the tower; Muthu asked for numbers he could write down.

facts.fact: Neela keeps a day-cloth cache in a dry crack under the lightning boulder, and Devan brings it warm inside his coat with rice and curd at grey.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her turn back at a cache below the boulder.

facts.fact: A Thurai raider sleeping by the tower has fresh salt-and-clove-bark resin on his skin and old pale ridged scars on the inside of both wrists, a long jaw and a ring on his left thumb. Neela does not know what it means (clue C12).
facts.why: needed because the beat plants C12: a resin that is not nightbark on scarred wrists.

facts.fact: Since Neela's self-naming no one can cage her without her own voice, so Devan's cheek-pebble is now a chosen ritual rather than a safeguard. The ration she smears came from the three noon trees Thilak tapped before leaving the shelter.
facts.why: needed because the beat frames the pebble as ritual, and it explains the thin resin supply.

facts.fact: An old woman refugee mends a net with a bone needle in a pass village on the cart road and stares at Neela's hands as Neela unconsciously ties the double hitch in her sash.
facts.why: needed because the beat ends on this encounter; the woman is unnamed here and is named in the next chapter.
